# `run_repeat`

the dot product and cosine of two runs' crossing directions per tile of one level.

Version 2, scope `subject`. Run it with `nxr-neuro run run_repeat --dataset <folder> --subject <id> ...`; `nxr-neuro run run_repeat --help` prints the same options.

Examples:

```
nxr-neuro run run_repeat --dataset <folder> --subject sub-01 --recording-a rest1 --recording-b rest2 --over "cortex tiles" --spatial-scale "parts 16"
```

## Inputs

| input | what it is | required |
|---|---|---|
| `recording_a` | field recording, where {"name": "$recording_a"} | yes |
| `recording_b` | field recording, where {"name": "$recording_b"} | yes |
| `over` | selection any, where {"name": "$over"} | yes |

## Parameters

Each is an option `--<name> VALUE` (dashes for underscores; the value is read as YAML) or `--set NAME=VALUE`.

| parameter | option | default | unit | choices | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `recording_a` | `--recording-a` | none | - |  | the first run (the statistics are of it); the order does not change the values |
| `recording_b` | `--recording-b` | none | - |  | the second run |
| `over` | `--over` | none | - |  | the grid both runs were measured over (<surface> tiles) |
| `spatial_scale` | `--spatial-scale` | none | mm |  | the tile level the crossings were measured at, as a quantity (a tile diameter in mm, a wavelength or parts per hemisphere) |
| `stage` | `--stage` | `0` | - |  | the stage by index: rows 2s and 2s+1 of the stored crossings (used when stage_name is null) |
| `stage_name` | `--stage-name` | none | - |  | the stage by name (burst, onset, within, offset), found in each run's own rows; refused when a run lacks it |
| `min_crossings` | `--min-crossings` | `10` | crossings |  | a tile counts when both runs have at least this many crossings (the senses pooled); nxr: 10 |
| `name` | `--name` | `vortex_cores.run_repeat.{recording_a}.{recording_b}` | - |  | the statistics' name (<name>.tiles, <name>.whole); give another for another stage |

## The chain of nodes

| phase | node | in | with | out |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| before | [`select.run_repeat`](../nodes.md) | a=recording_a, b=recording_b, over=over | spatial_scale=$spatial_scale, stage=$stage, stage_name=$stage_name, min_crossings=$min_crossings | tiles, whole |

## Outputs

| output | stored as |
|---|---|
| `tiles` | kind statistic, name $name.tiles, of recording_a, over over, axes [{"name": "tile"}] |
| `whole` | kind statistic, name $name.whole, of recording_a, over over, axes [{"name": "whole"}] |

## Notes from the definition

```text
THE RUN-TO-RUN REPEAT OF THE VORTEX CORES' CROSSINGS (two statistics of the first run): does each tile's direction of core movement repeat from one recording to the next? Read from the two
runs' stored `tile_crossings` (the measurements `run vortex_cores` stored over the same tile level), never a recording: per tile the dot product of the two runs' mean resultant crossing
vectors (the senses pooled), for the tiles with at least `min_crossings` crossings in both runs, and, for the whole recording, the count-weighted mean cosine of the tiles' directions.
  <name>.tiles   measure repeat_dot, method run_repeat, [tiles] (NaN where a run has fewer crossings); the axis is the level's Selection
  <name>.whole   measure repeat_cosine, method run_repeat, [1]
WHAT IT CANNOT SAY: a p-value (a tile's dot against the lag-free surrogate draws', Benjamini-Hochberg over the tiles) needs the lag-free surrogate (`run surrogate_lagfree_vortex_compare`): this is the statistic only. Two runs of one subject share
the cortex, the kernel and the instrument's leakage, so their agreement is evidence only against that null.

  nxr-neuro run run_repeat --dataset <folder> --subject sub-01 --recording-a rest1 --recording-b rest2 --over "cortex tiles" --spatial-scale "parts 16"
```
